reviews.evidence: BUF outshot DAL 26-18 but lost 4-0. Luukkonen let in 4 goals on 18 shots, and Oettinger got his second straight shutout (NHL.com/ESPN). The goalie gap decided it. rkGsax (+0.86) still leaned BUF though Luukkonen's saved (-0.048) was poor, and the model sat 9 pts above market.

Drysdale played 23:15 on the top pair with Sanheim, with 2:17 on the power play, and StatMuse shows 3 shots. The model's 0.54 mean leaned on a 0.25 recent rate from 4 games. The market priced the under at only 57%, so the role hadn't changed and the small-sample recent term dragged the projection down.

Toronto led 3-0 by 8:37 of the 1st (Roslovic at 0:34, Cowan at 3:20, Paul at 8:37). Trailing Vegas then pushed for the rest of the game, which went to overtime and a shootout, and outshot Toronto 43-24. Bobrovsky made 40 saves (NHL.com/ESPN recaps).

Buffalo outshot Dallas 26-18, but Luukkonen gave up 4 goals on 18 shots and Oettinger stopped all 26 for his second straight shutout. The AP and NHL.com recaps mention no injuries, scratches or lineup changes, so this looks like finishing and goaltending variance.

Vegas trailed Toronto by three goals and rallied to win 4-3 in a shootout, so the game went to overtime and Vegas spent a long stretch chasing. In that game Barbashev took 4 shots on 18:34 of ice time, against a projected mean of 1.36.

Hagel kept his full role: 22:55 TOI with 3:29 on the power play in a close 3-2 TB win (ESPN). He recorded 3 shots, one short of the 3.5 line, and the ESPN play-by-play shows two of them went wide. No injury, lineup or script change turned up.

Fowler's usage was normal (20:13 TOI, 0:53 on the power play) and he got 3 assists in a 5-4 game. Two Blues goals came late while trailing 5-2, one of them short-handed. The under drifted from -235 to -190 at close, but I found no news behind the move.

Both of Jones's points were secondary assists on Sam Reinhart's two power-play goals in the 2nd period of a 5-3 loss at BUF (ESPN). He played 4:18 on the PP, below his 6.09 average, so his role was steady. The model gave the over a 39% chance, and it landed.

The NHL.com preview said Colorado would dress 11 forwards and 7 defensemen (Juulsen as the extra D), with Makar back and Malinski on the second pair. He played 14:23 TOI with 0:10 on the PP, versus the model's 17.6 min and 0.39 PP share, and took 0 shot attempts.

Hyry's only point was an unassisted shorthanded breakaway goal at 3rd-period 1:20, after he stole the puck from Makar (NHL.com recap). He played 14:40 with no power-play time, which fits the role the model assumed. It's an unusual way to score, not a change in his role.

Kucherov's usage was normal: 22:16 TOI and 4:18 on the power play, about the 21 minutes and 5.3 PP minutes projected. Previews and the ESPN/Yahoo recaps show no lineup change. A short OT (Hedman scored at 2:07 for a 4-3 win) added little. 8 shots on a 2.72 mean is a tail result.

Maccelli kept the same job: top line with Horvat and first power-play unit, with Barzal out (the model knew). He played 15:26 with 4:07 on the PP, a bit over his 3.06 average. His 5 shots and a goal in the 3-2 win look like a tail result, not a missed change.

Desharnais got two second-period assists (on Protas's and Jenner's goals) in a 4-2 win, his first multi-point game since March 2024 per CBS. He played 20:23 with 0:00 on the power play and 0 shots. The model already had Roy and Sandin out, so this was a tail result for a low-scoring defenseman.

Killorn played his usual job: third line with Poehling, as the NHL.com preview projected, 18:37 TOI, 3:27 on the PK. He had 4 shots in a 4-2 win. The under went from -115 to +130 at close, but no news explains it, and the inputs looked right.

CBS Sports (Oct 13) said Protas had 2 assists in 6 games in a deep WSH lineup and gets no PP time. He played 0:02 on the PP in this game. The model still put 0.727 weight on last season's 0.59 rate over his 0.2 recent rate.

Rasmus Dahlin (averaging 26:32 TOI) left the Oct 12 game with an upper-body injury and sat this one (TSN). Zellweger played 24:28 against the model's 19-minute projection. The model listed Dahlin as out but left vacF at 1, so his minutes never went to Zellweger.

Dobson played 22:21 (vs 21.2 projected) with Matheson out, and only 0:18 on the power play. That role was in line with the inputs, and the 5-4 one-goal game wasn't a lopsided script. ESPN's play-by-play shows him getting shots on Lindgren, so the 5 SOG looks like a tail result.

The NHL.com recap shows Reinhart scored both his goals on the power play in a 5-3 loss. The first was a Seth Jones shot that trickled through Ellis's pads and Reinhart poked it in. His usage matched the model's inputs (20:27 TOI, 4:54 on the PP), so nothing in his role was missed.

WSH outshot SEA 36-27 and Daccord stopped 33, including 17 in the third, while Thompson saved 22 of 27. McCann's go-ahead goal came with 5:27 left. Both starters were as expected and nothing changed beforehand. Carbery blamed puck mistakes (WSH had 20 giveaways). Source: NHL.com recap.

Swayman (36 saves) and Vejmelka started as the model expected. BOS drifted +105 to +120 at close, with Utah -125 in previews, and I found no injury or lineup news behind the move. Boston won 6-1 on 3 PP goals from 22 shots.

Pregame previews had Laviolette reshuffling LA's lines, with Haula moving to wing (Byfield/Moore line or Laughton line) and the Kings dressing 11 forwards and 7 D, which means more ice time per forward. The under drifted from +100 to +120 at close, and the model never repriced on LA's lineup. Haula still had just 1 shot in 15:08.

Per NHL.com and Miami Herald recaps, Tkachuk had no goals in 6 FLA games, then scored a natural hat trick (1 EV, 2 PP, on 4 shots) plus an assist. His role was normal: 16:19 TOI, 5:23 PP. Talbot was pulled after allowing 6 goals. A 4-point game is a tail result, not a missed input.

Zetterlund played only 11:26 overall, but 3:50 of it was on the power play, about twice the model's ppTime of 1.79. With Ottawa missing several players, he got extra PP work and took 4 shots (CBS gametracker box score).

Holloway played 23:15 TOI against the 17.3 minutes the model used and finished with 3 shots. STL had Buchnevich, Dube, Toropchenko and Trudeau out, but vac=0.109 was left at vacF=1. NHL.com recap: STL trailed 5-2 late, and Holloway scored with the goalie pulled.

Necas's role held: 22:24 TOI and 5:20 on the power play, above the model's 21.2 minutes and 4.71 PP. He still had 0 shots and 0 misses in a close 3-2 shootout game, per the ESPN box. I found no news of a role change, injury or matchup plan that would explain it.

Novak played 15:16 TOI with 1:50 on the power play, close to the model's 15.2 minutes and 2.27 PP minutes, but still took 4 shots against a 1.48 mean. The ESPN recap of the Avs' 5-2 rally win shows no role or lineup change.

The NHL.com recap says Blackwood made 29 saves as COL came back from 0-2 to win 5-2. Both starting goalies were confirmed and no lineup, role or line news came out. Trailing Pittsburgh outshooting COL fits the model's script term, so 29 vs the 22.45 projection is about a 1 SD tail result.

Edmonton went up 3-0 in the first period on just 7 shots, and LA pulled Kuemper after 20:00 with 4 saves. The Oilers had only 17 shots in the whole game, so his save total was cut short by being pulled early, not by a wrong rate or role.

Per the AP recap, Boldy had a hat trick and 4 points on the top line with Kaprizov and Eriksson Ek, playing 24:51 TOI and 5:38 on the power play. That is his normal top-line role. The model already gave the Over 59%, so this was a likely outcome landing in the high tail.

Chatfield's usage was normal: 21:01 TOI and only 0:22 on the power play, with 0 shots. He picked up a single secondary assist on Jankowski's 3rd-period goal (15:09) that made it 4-1 in a game CAR controlled, according to the ESPN box score. The bet lost on a 22% tail outcome.

Daccord started as expected and Ryan Lindgren had been on IR since Oct 8, so the inputs were right. Florida led 6-2 after two periods (ESPN), outshot SEA 37-23 and went 2-for-3 on the power play. Hat tricks from Verhaeghe and Bennett made it a tail result.

The Under won (0 shots in 17:42 TOI; a double-minor took him off the ice). The price only went from -150 to -145, about 0.9 pts. McAvoy came back from suspension (insidetherink), which points toward the Under, so I found no news behind the move. It looks like noise.

Anaheim scored first and went up 2-0 early in the 2nd, then rode the lead in a low-event game. The Ducks took only 16 shots on Stevenson (12 saves) and the Jets managed just 16 on Dostal (ABC7/TSN recaps). The model's script factor of 0.983 barely cut his shot volume.

The Under won (Meier had 0 points, 0 SOG, 14:38 TOI, 0:42 PP, in a 4-1 loss). The 'miss' was only a small CLV slip, -145 to -140. The NHL preview had Meier on the top line with Hischier and Evangelista, and no news explains the move.

Tuch (WSH) had 3 points in a 5-4 win: an assist on Kyrou's 1st-period goal, an unassisted shorthanded goal and an unassisted goal at 17:05 of the 3rd. His usage was normal (18:49 TOI). The model had it near 50/50, so this is a tail result. (ESPN/NHL.com)

The box score shows S=4 but SOG=0 and SM=3. ESPN's play-by-play lists Hartman's attempts as blocked (by Bennett) or wide (a tip-in wide left). So 4 counts shot attempts, not shots on goal. With 0 SOG the Under 1.5 should have won.
reviews.bug: The bet was graded on the box score's 'S' field (4 shot attempts: blocked plus missed) instead of 'SOG' (0). This marked a winning Under 1.5 Shots as lost.

reviews.evidence: The model assumed 17.3 minutes. Burns played 13:39 (11:02 at even strength, 2:37 shorthanded, 0:00 on the power play). His attempts went wide or were blocked, per the ESPN play-by-play. Less ice time on a third-pair, penalty-kill job made 2+ shots unlikely.

The model had the right starters (Wedgewood, Cooley) and shots were an even 30-29, so volume wasn't the issue. Cooley gave up 7 goals on 30 shots, including screened point shots and deflections off Middleton, while CGY scored twice in 71 seconds late. That's finishing variance, not a missed input.

Texier's role matched the model: 14:36 TOI, 1:32 PP, and he was in the shootout. Montreal outshot Buffalo 38-17 (CBS box), and 5 shots in under 15 minutes is a tail result. One oddity: the box feed lists S=5 but SOG=0.

Anaheim led most of the game and won 5-1, so they barely shot: Stevenson made just 12 saves, meaning about 17 Ducks shots on goal in total (TSN recap). Sennecke's minutes were normal (17:03 TOI, 1:49 PP) and he still had 0 SOG, with 2 shots missed.

Zegras logged 19:25 TOI with 4:03 on the PP and assisted on Michkov's PP goal in OTT's 2-1 win (ESPN). His usual top-6/PP1 role was unchanged. The model's mean of 0.88 leaned on a 0.5 recent rate over 4 games, which is far below his normal ~2 shots per game.

Hagel's role was normal: 21:32 TOI, 4:34 on the power play, 6 shots. His 4 points came from a hat trick with 2 goals in the last 1:44, one into an empty net (ESPN/AP recap). The model's own mean was 1.04 points and the line didn't move, so this was a tail outcome, not a missed input.

Rust kept his usual spot with Rakell and Crosby on the top line (NHL.com preview) and played 18:38 with 1:42 PP against the 19.1 projected. He had 2 SOG, so the Under won. The close only moved from -165 to -155, with no news behind it.

Toronto led 3-0 within 8:37, then sat back as Vegas outshot them 43-24 (CBS recap). Tavares's line was pinned in its own zone on the 3-1 and 3-2 goals (Hot Stove). He played 15:26 with 0 SOG and 1 miss, below the 0.936 script term.

Kane's role held: top line with Lardis and Greene after Nazar's suspension (Second City Hockey), 18:17 TOI and 2:14 on the PP. His 5 shots were a big share of Chicago's 26, so this looks like a tail result, not a role change.

InsideTheRink's preview had Quinn on the top line with Thompson and Norris and on PP1 with Zucker out. He played 4:39 on the PP against the model's 3.44, had a PP assist on Ostlund's go-ahead goal, and the under drifted from -110 to +110.

The bet won (0 points), but the price moved from -526 to -360. Duchene's surgery made Hyry Dallas's 3rd-line center between Back and Seguin (THW, NHL.com preview). The model had Duchene listed out but role was null and vac=0. Hyry played 13:31, with no PP time.

Per ESPN and NHL.com, Zacha's 2 points were both secondary assists on 3rd-period power-play goals (Pastrnak 3:26, Lindholm 8:18). His usage looked normal: 17:04 TOI, 2:42 PP time vs the 2.1 the model expected. No role or lineup change found.

Evans played a normal 20:02 TOI with 0:05 on the power play. His only point was a secondary assist on McCann's go-ahead even-strength goal at 14:33 of the 3rd (ESPN summary). His role and inputs were as expected, so a single assist landing in the 24% tail is variance.

Voronkov was in his usual spot on the third line (Nichushkin-Monahan-Voronkov) and the second power-play unit, playing 12:43 with 1:41 on the PP. Columbus outshot Pittsburgh 45-22 in a close shootout game, and he had 5 shots, far in the tail of a 1.19 mean.

Verhaeghe's role was normal: 17:05 TOI and 2:33 on the power play. He scored twice in 71 seconds late in the 1st, while it was 1-1, so the 8-3 blowout came after. He scored 3 goals on 5 shots, a tail result. The under was close to a coin flip at 0.50 (Yahoo/THN recaps).

ESPN box: Brodin's only point was a second assist on Kaprizov's 1st-period goal, with Quinn Hughes on the first assist. He played 21:39 with no power-play time, his usual role, so the 1 point fell in the tail. The price drifted from -417 to -320, but I found no news behind it.

The model had Joey Daccord starting for SEA, but the AP recap (KOMO) shows Philipp Grubauer started and made 38 saves. The total also fell from 6.5 to 5.5 before close, so the model lost the closing line even though the Over won with 9 goals.
reviews.bug: Wrong away starter: the model used Joey Daccord's saved/vsUsual/gsax inputs, but Philipp Grubauer started for Seattle.

reviews.evidence: CBS confirms Harley had 7 SOG in 25:08 on Dallas's 25 shots, playing his previewed second-pair and PP2 role with no lineup news. Seven is a tail result even at the market's higher fair over (0.51). The model's low rate (1.06) and recent (0.75) may also have understated him.

Aho got his full role: 20:51 TOI, 2:46 on the power play, in a close 3-2 CAR win (NHL.com/ESPN recaps). He had 0 SOG and 0 missed shots, and ESPN's play-by-play shows his attempts blocked (one by Iafallo). I found no role, injury or script change, so this is a tail result.

Florida was expected to win by about 1 but trailed most of the game. They tied it with 13 seconds left in the 3rd and won in OT (NHL.com recap). Bennett played 19:55 against the 18.3 projected, almost all at even strength, and the time spent chasing likely drove his 6 shots.

The bet won: Barkey had 1 assist (on Seeler's goal) in 15:19 TOI with 3:17 of power-play time, so his role was as expected. The price drifted from +180 to +210 with no line, lineup or injury news found. The Flyers were 0-5-2 and scored only once in a 4-1 loss.

Dubois (illness), whom the model listed as questionable, was confirmed out, per RMNB. Sourdif stayed a 4th-line center. The price drifting from -227 to -200 likely reflects that news. The under still cashed: 0 points, 16:05 TOI, 0:09 PP time.

Nylander played his usual top-six and PP1 role (19:51 TOI, 4:11 PPTOI) and scored 2G and 3A, tying his career high, in a 6-3 TOR win (AP recap). Nothing shows a role, injury or line change. Note the model's own under chance (0.365) was below fair (0.406), so it took a -EV bet.

NHL.com recap: Murashov made 43 saves, 23 in the 2nd period, as CBJ 'controlled the pace' start to finish while PIT managed ~20 shots on Talbot. I found no injury, lineup change or line move to explain the extra shots; OT added only a few.

Vegas fell behind 3-0 early and pushed to come back, and the game went to overtime. Eichel played 26:38, including 6:39 on the power play, and got 6 shots while chasing (CTV recap). The model's script term of 1.125 underrated how far behind Vegas would get and the extra time.

Before the game, NHL.com and Sportsnaut both projected Greer on Anaheim's top line with Carlsson and Gauthier. The model had no role input (role null), and the under price moved from -245 to -175 by close. Greer played only 12:33 and finished with 0 points, so the bet won.

Bennett had no larger role: 12:25 TOI, 0:00 on the power play, a usual even-strength load. He still scored 3 even-strength goals, his first of the season, in an 8-3 Panthers blowout where FLA outshot SEA 38-23 (Sofascore recap). That is finishing in the tail, not a usage change.

Nylander had 5 SOG in 20:31 TOI (1:54 on the PP), which is his normal workload. Vegas won 4-3 in a shootout after coming back from 3 down (CBS/NHL.com recaps). The short overtime added a little ice time, but I found no role, lineup or injury change.

The model bet Over 6.5 at +110, but the line it saw at 21:44Z was 5.5 (-122) and the game closed at 5.5 (-125). BetMGM's preview listed the total near 6. The 6.5 line doesn't match the market, which is why CLV shows a 1-point, 10% loss. The final was 4-1, a total of 5.
reviews.bug: The bet was recorded or priced at 6.5 +110, but the market line the model saw and the close were both 5.5. The bet line looks stale, mismatched or an alternate line, so the CLV is comparing two differ

reviews.evidence: Pettersson played a normal shutdown role: 21:44 TOI, 3:55 on the PK, basically no power play time and 0 shots on goal. He picked up 2 secondary assists in the 4-1 win (one on Cuylle's goal, per Yahoo). I found no role or lineup change, so this was a tail result.

Hartman centered his usual Coleman-Hartman-Brink line (THN preview) and played 13:48 with 3:04 PP, close to the model's 14.9 min. The under moved +105→+125 but I found no news behind it; the Wild's 3 F/3 D/G injuries were already known before the game.

Previews from NHL.com and Inside the Rink had Karlsson on the 2nd line with Cotter and Rossi, as the model expected. The close only moved from -115 to -110 at 1.5, and I found no news behind it. He had 3 shots and the over won.

Larsson's one point was a secondary assist on Kakko's even-strength goal at 6:06 of the 1st (ESPN summary). He played his usual minutes, 24:43 TOI with only 0:05 on the power play, so his role was unchanged. The model gave this about a 20% chance; it just happened.

The AP, NHL.com and FLM recaps of WSH's 5-4 win say nothing about Wilson's role, lineup or injuries. His box shows 5 shots in 17:13 of ice time, less than the 19.8 min projected. PP time was 3:47 vs 2.31 projected, a small bump. The line moved to 1.5 at close, so the market didn't move against the under.

Hagens played 11:17 (1:29 on the power play), less than the 12.5 minutes the model projected, and still got 2 shots, just over the 1.5 line. The model's mean of 1.64 sat close to the line. BOS won 4-1 (NHL.com, 98.5 recaps), not a blowout, and I found no role or lineup change.

ESPN recap: MIN scored 3 in the 1st, outshot VGK 23-11 through two periods and won 4-2. Wallstedt stopped 21 of 23 and Hart 24 of 28, as expected. VGK went 0-for-5 on the PP against the NHL's top PK. Nothing specific was missed on a near coin-flip line.

Coyle played 23:30 TOI, 6:01 of it on the power play (Inside The Rink's preview had him on PP1), over 2 OTs plus a shootout, and took 7 shots. The model ran with no role term (role null) and a 1.13 rate from just 2 games. Caveat: the box lists SOG as 0, so the 7 may count attempts.
